props.gloss_en: a ewe that had not given birth bore two males and both heads emerged as one -- R' Yosei HaGelili: both are the kohen's
as it is said: 'the males shall be the Lord's' (Shemot 13:12)
the Sages: it is impossible to be exact [that the two coincide]
rather, one is his and one is the kohen's
R' Tarfon: the kohen chooses the better one for himself
R' Akiva: they assess [the two] between them
and the second grazes until it becomes blemished
and [the second] is obligated in the gifts
and R' Yosei exempts [it from the gifts]
if one of them died -- R' Tarfon: they divide [the survivor]
R' Akiva: the one who would extract from his fellow bears the burden of proof
a male and a female -- the kohen has nothing here

supports.gloss_en: אי אפשר לצמצם, אלא אחד לו ואחד לכהן -- since the two cannot have emerged at exactly the same moment, one of them is the firstborn
